comments.body:
## Measurement detail (moved out of the description under the P4 admission cap)

### Field weights of the CURRENT lean payload — 2,855 tickets, this store

| field | bytes | share of lean |
|---|---:|---:|
| `authorship_ledger` | 26,241,422 | 59% |
| `attestations` | 10,370,251 | 23% |
| `signature` | 2,639,114 | 6% |
| `keyring` | ~0 (empty on all but a signed-keyring ticket) | <0.1% |
| everything else | 5,141,280 | 12% |

Lean total 44,392,067 B at 15,548 B/row; after the widened projection 4,928,872 B at
1,726 B/row. Lean-vs-full before this change was 44.4 MB vs 73.0 MB — a 39% saving that
left the actual bulk untouched, which is why the docstring's "stays small" was literally
true and materially false.

`keyring` is dropped on a consistency argument, not a size one. It is the fourth member of
the same per-ticket signing record as the three measured fields; retaining exactly one
member of that record on a discovery row would make `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` an arbitrary set
rather than "the signing record plus the bodies", and the next reader could not derive it.

### Per-query effect

| query | lean before | lean after |
|---|---:|---:|
| unfiltered (2,855) | 44,392,067 | 4,928,872 |
| `status=open` (51) | 224,610 | 58,867 |
| `in_progress` (15) | 182,426 | 24,392 |
| `tag=mcp,status=open,type=bug` (10) | 52,854 | 11,178 |
| `ready` (61) | 693,556 | 76,878 |

### CLI surface, measured for the breaking-change note

`rebar list --status closed`, 2,696 rows, key counts read off the same ticket
(`0024-fa99-d5bb-49bc`) in each run: 39 keys -> 35 (losing exactly `authorship_ledger`,
`attestations`, `signature`, `keyring`), 43,661,976 -> 4,747,485 bytes, a 9.2x reduction.
`--full` restores all four plus the two bodies (41 keys, 71,707,799 bytes).

### Provenance

These figures were taken on 2026-08-28 during the root-cause phase of
`daughterly-agitative-ocelot` (`494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0`), whose Phase 1 and Phase 4 comments
carry the original runs. This story is the projection half of that fix, split out so the
bound and the projection are reviewable independently.

comments.body:
## Gerrit change 2354 — "Make the lean discovery row actually lean"

`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2354`. NOT submitted.

Split out of Gerrit 2336, which carried both halves of the `daughterly-agitative-ocelot` fix
and could not pass plan review: its AC-2 had to argue one shared projection, two backends, an
untouched library, an MCP-layer application point, three narrowing surfaces and three
unaffected consumers inside a single bullet, at 7,678 of the 8,000-char admission cap. 2336 is
marked WIP with a supersession note.

### What landed

`LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` + `lean_projection` in `_engine_support/reads.py` are the one spelling of
the lean row, dropping `authorship_ledger`/`attestations`/`signature`/`keyring` as well as the
two bodies. `_snapshot/ticket_view.py` calls the same function. `ready_tickets` gains
`full: bool = False` and projects through it via `_discovery_rows`. The golden-path probe's
show-vs-list drift assertion is repaired and now DERIVES its expectation. Breaking-change notes
for the three narrowing surfaces in `docs/release-notes.md` + `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Blast radius, re-verified from source

Six consumers reach the lean path; **three narrow**, and the narrowing comes from each
CALLER's own flag default, never the library's:

- CLI `rebar list` — `"include_body": ns.full` (`reads_cli.py:286`), `--full` defaults False.
- MCP `list_tickets` — its own `full: bool = False` (`_mcp_reads.py:291`).
- MCP `ready_tickets` — new here.

**Unaffected:** the LIBRARY `rebar.list_tickets`, whose own `full` defaults **True**
(`_lib_reads.py:128`) — a direct library call still returns the full shape; `validate.py:67`
(2,863 rows, `query=None` -> default `TicketQuery()`); `next_batch.py:144` (62 rows,
`include_body` unset). `show_state` / `search_state` never call `list_states` at all.

The plan-review gate BLOCKED an earlier revision for getting exactly this wrong — the first
draft claimed the library default narrows. It does not. Corrected before the review passed.

### Verification

- Backend parity tested against a real pinned view, both directions (parity + `include_body=True`
  still carries the bodies), using a parent-bounded query because `list_by_query` raises
  `UnsupportedPinnedQuery` on a parentless one.
- Both discovery surfaces asserted to agree on their default key set.
- Mutation check: shrinking `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` back to the two body fields turns 3 shape
  tests RED and the golden-path probe from 142/0 to 141/1.
- `make lint` (ratchet `active=39 new=0 increased=0`), `make typecheck` (685 files),
  `pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces` 7,747 passed, `probe_rebar.py` 142/0.

### Attestation

Plan review PASSED and signed at `25ea12c2`. It has since gone `stale-code` because
`CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/release-notes.md` moved on `origin/main` (unrelated entries from other
changes landing) — the claim it authorised already happened, and change 2354 earned
`LLM-Review +1` on patch set 1.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The lean discovery row is not lean. `include_body=False` drops only `description` and
`comments`, leaving four base64 DSSE signature fields in every row. Measured on this store
(2,855 tickets), three of them carry **88% of a lean list's bytes** — `authorship_ledger`
26,241,422 B (59%), `attestations` 10,370,251 B (23%), `signature` 2,639,114 B (6%) — so a
lean list is 44,392,067 B at 15,548 B/row. The fourth, `keyring`, measures ~0 and is dropped
for **consistency, not size**: it is the fourth member of the same per-ticket signing record,
and keeping one member on a discovery row would make the drop set arbitrary. Dropping all
four gives 4,928,872 B and 1,726 B/row, a 9x reduction. (Full table in the measurement
comment.)

A list caller is choosing a ticket. The signing record is read per-ticket via `show` /
`verify-signature`, which are untouched. Two backends spell the lean row separately today
(`_engine_support/reads.py::list_states` and `_snapshot/ticket_view.py::list_by_query`), so
they can drift.

This is the prerequisite for the response-budget bound on `daughterly-agitative-ocelot`
(`494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0`): without this projection a 90,000-byte bound would refuse even
`list_tickets(status="open")` (51 rows, 224,610 lean bytes). It is independently valuable
without that bound and lands first.

## Blast radius — every consumer of the lean path

`lean_projection` is reached only from `list_states` and `TicketView.list_by_query`, and only
when `include_body` is False. **`TicketQuery.include_body` defaults `True`**
(`_engine_support/ticket_query.py:52`), so a caller that does not ask for a lean row is
unaffected. The six call sites, each verified by reading it:

| # | consumer | how it builds the query | narrows? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CLI `rebar list` (`reads_cli.py:344`) | `"include_body": ns.full` (`:286`) — the CLI's OWN `--full` defaults False | **YES** |
| 2 | library `rebar.list_tickets` (`_lib_reads.py:166`) | `include_body=full`, and `full: bool = True` (`_lib_reads.py:128`) | **NO — the library default does not narrow** |
| 3 | MCP `list_tickets` (`_mcp_reads.py:291`) | its OWN `full: bool = False`, forwarded through (2) | **YES** |
| 4 | MCP `ready_tickets` (`_mcp_reads.py:349`) | `rebar.ready(sort=...)`; no `include_body` plumbing at all | **YES — new, see below** |
| 5 | `_engine_support/validate.py:67` | `list_states(tracker)` — `query=None` builds a default `TicketQuery()` | NO — `include_body=True` |
| 6 | `_engine_support/next_batch.py:144` | `TicketQuery(status="open,in_progress")` — `include_body` unset | NO — `include_body=True` |

**The narrowing comes from each CALLER's own flag default, never from the library's.**
`rebar.list_tickets(status="open")` with no `full` argument keeps returning the FULL shape
after this change; only the CLI's `--full` and the MCP tool's `full=False` select a lean row.
A direct library consumer is therefore not broken, so the breaking-change note covers exactly
the CLI and the two MCP tools.

(5) reduces 2,863 rows and (6) 62 rows; both keep all four fields, so neither the repo-health
validator nor conflict-aware batching loses input. `show_state` and `search_state`
(`reads.py:338`, `:527`) never call `list_states` — `search` has its own
`project_search_result` projection — so `show`, `rebar show`, `show_ticket` and `search` are
untouched on every surface.

Three surfaces narrow: CLI `rebar list`, MCP `list_tickets`, MCP `ready_tickets`.

## `ready_tickets`: the default narrows, deliberately

On `origin/main` `ready_tickets(sort)` (`_mcp_reads.py:349`) returns the FULL shape with no
opt-out, so a lean default narrows a published, schema-pinned MCP read. Three options:

- **(a) keep the full default, add `full` as an opt-IN to lean.** Rejected: it leaves the two
  discovery surfaces disagreeing on their default shape for no benefit to any caller, and it
  strands `ready_tickets` at 693,556 bytes for 61 rows — the largest unbounded read here.
- **(b) narrow the default, add `full=True` as the opt-OUT, document the break.** CHOSEN.
- **(c) leave `ready_tickets` alone entirely.** Rejected for the same reason as (a).

The library is deliberately NOT changed: `rebar.ready(*, sort, repo_root)` ->
`ready_states(tracker, *, epic, sort)` -> `public_state` has no `include_body`/`full` plumbing
and this story adds none. The projection happens one layer up in the MCP tool, through the
SAME `lean_projection`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **One shared projection.** `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` + `lean_projection` in
      `_engine_support/reads.py` are the only spelling of the lean row, dropping
      `authorship_ledger`, `attestations`, `signature`, `keyring` as well as `description` and
      `comments`. Both backends call it: `list_states` and
      `_snapshot/ticket_view.py::TicketView.list_by_query`.
- [x] **Backend parity is TESTED, not asserted.** A test runs the same `TicketQuery` through
      both backends against a real pinned view over a real tracker and asserts identical key
      sets (kills "one backend stopped projecting"); a second asserts `include_body=True`
      still carries the bodies on both (kills "a backend projects unconditionally"). **The
      query MUST be parent-bounded** — `TicketView.list_by_query` raises
      `UnsupportedPinnedQuery` on a parentless query and on any `min_children`/`blocking_state`
      query (`_snapshot/ticket_view.py:350`, `:354`), so a parentless shared query would raise
      on the snapshot backend instead of projecting and the parity assertion would never run.
      Concretely: a story parent plus one child task carrying a description and a comment,
      queried as `TicketQuery(parent=<parent>, include_body=False)`.
- [x] **`ready_tickets` gains `full: bool = False`**, projecting through `lean_projection`;
      `full=True` returns exactly the previous bytes. No library signature changes.
- [x] **Both discovery surfaces agree on their default shape**, asserted directly: the same
      rows through `list_tickets` and `ready_tickets` produce the same key set. They reach
      `lean_projection` by different routes (read core vs MCP tool layer), so sharing a
      function is only a claim until something compares the two outputs.
- [x] **The CLI drift probe is repaired and stays a drift detector.** `scripts/probe_rebar.py`
      asserts the exact symmetric difference between `rebar show` and `rebar list` key sets in
      both directions; widening the drop set changes `rebar list`, so the probe must be
      updated. Its expectation is DERIVED (show-only computed fields, plus the lean-dropped set
      INTERSECTED with what `show` actually emits) rather than hardcoded, because
      `authorship_ledger`/`attestations` materialise only once a ticket has signature material
      — an empty tracker's `show` carries neither.
- [x] **The three narrowing surfaces are recorded as pre-1.0 breaking changes** in
      `docs/release-notes.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, each with measured before/after and the
      opt-out, and the note states the LIBRARY default is unchanged. CLI
      `rebar list --status closed` (2,696 rows) is measured explicitly because it is a
      USER-visible change, not an agent-only one.
- [x] **Mutation-checked.** Shrinking `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` back to the two body fields must
      turn the shape tests and the probe RED.

## Definition of Done

- `make lint` (ruff + format-check + complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0`), `make typecheck`,
  `pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces` green.
- `python scripts/probe_rebar.py` green (it fails 141/1 before the repair).
- Change pushed to Gerrit, `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.

## Non-goals

- The MCP response-size bound, `_mcp_budget.py`, and the `response_too_large` refusal — those
  are `494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0`, which depends on this.
- A narrower discovery-specific output model — that is `lucky-egoistic-akitainu`
  (`0c99-8f2b-0de7-48f2`).

file_impact.reason: LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS + lean_projection: the ONE spelling of the lean list row, now dropping the signature material as well as the two bodies.
Snapshot read backend calls the same lean_projection so the two backends cannot drift.
ready_tickets gains full: bool = False and projects through the shared lean_projection via the new _discovery_rows helper; list_tickets docstring records the widened drop set.
The show-vs-list key-set drift assertion is derived from the lean drop set rather than hardcoded, because widening it narrows CLI rebar list too.
Backend parity tests: same query through both backends, identical key sets; include_body=True still carries the bodies on both.
New: the lean-shape regression tests for list_tickets and ready_tickets over a real store.
Pre-1.0 breaking-change note for the three narrowing surfaces with measured before/after.
Same breaking change recorded in the curated changelog.

compiled_state.title: Make the lean discovery row actually lean: one shared projection across both read backends
